canonical.title: Insert Into a Binary Search Tree
canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/2. Practice Problems/03. Insert into BST.cpp

narrative.title: Onboarding the New Filing Cabinet
narrative.scenario: A compliance office files every contract by value in a sorted tree, and a brand-new contract arrives that matches nothing on file. Rather than reorganizing the archive, the clerk walks the tree once — smaller goes left, larger goes right — until a corridor dead-ends, and hangs the new contract exactly there. The archive's shape grows by one leaf; nothing else moves.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) and an integer val to insert. val does not already exist in the tree.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the tree after insertion, serialized as a level-order array with trailing nulls trimmed.
constraints: All values are unique before and after insertion

testCases.explanation: 5 descends right of 4, left of 7, and becomes 7's left child.
Inserting into an empty archive creates the root.

hintLevels: Level 1: A new record always lands as a leaf — the walk itself chooses the corridor.
Level 2: Recurse left when the newcomer is smaller, right when larger; a null pointer is the landing spot.
Level 3: Rewire on the way back up: child = insert(child, val) keeps the return-value chain intact, and an empty tree becomes the new root.
